patch_description: The current program's bottleneck is a slow stochastic hill climb plus a single SLSQP pass from few seeds (score 1.00). The new approach replaces the hill climb with analytic-gradient ascent on a smoothed version of the true objective: both the min and max of the 91 squared pairwise distances are replaced by log-sum-exp smoothings, with temperature annealed from 0.3 down to 0.04 (matching Gen 11's fast core), optimized with Adam (lr 0.02). The exact gradient of the smooth ratio dmin_s/dmax_s is accumulated over the pairwise-distance matrix. This is ~20x faster per unit quality, so I spend the freed budget on ~30 diverse seeds (random spheres, antipodal pairs, icosahedron+2 extras, Fibonacci sphere, cube+center+extras) and then run the exact SLSQP formulation (maximize t s.t. t ≤ |xi−xj|² ≤ 1) on the top 10 smoothed results with maxiter 300, plus a final SLSQP restart round on the best solution. Key parameters: Adam lr=0.02, tau schedule 0.3→0.04 over 350 iters, 30 seeds, top-10 SLSQP refinement, second polish round.
